newsitem.title: USA: Junk issues price, 10-year corporate debt tightens.
newsitem.headline: Junk issues price, 10-year corporate debt tightens.

text.p: A pair of high-yield bond issues topped an otherwise quiet session on Tuesday, while investment grade corporate bonds tightened marginally in the 10-year sector, dealers across both markets said.

Leading the junk slate, oil and gas concern Forcenergy Inc increased its 10-year senior subordinated note offering by $25 million to $200 million. The notes were priced with a 8-1/2 percent coupon to yield 220 basis points over Treasuries.
Most proceeds will be used to pay down all outstanding debt under the company's revolving credit facility, said company spokesman J. Russell Porter.

The remainder will supplement the anticipated difference between 1997 cash flow and projected capital spending, he said. Forcenergy in January said it planned to spend about $195 million on 1997 capital projects, excluding acquisitions, which would be pursued opportunistically throughout the year.
Forcenergy's new issue was bid up more than one point at 100-3/8 near the close. Salomon Brothers was lead manager.
Also on Tuesday, Barrett Resources issued $150 million 10-year senior notes with a 7.55 percent coupon to yield 118 basis points over Treasuries via Goldman, Sachs & Co.
Turning to secondary high-yield trade, grocery sector bonds, including Grand Union Co, Ralphs Grocery and Penn Traffic Co rose by one point on average.

Investment grade corporate bond trade was moderate throughout the session with prices unchanged to firmer in spots, traders said. The lack of new issuance and commencement of the government's quarterly refunding effectively capped action, they said.
Traders reported marginal spread tightening in the 10-year sector as buyers emerged in anticipation of the government's auction and ensuing 10-year roll.

In company specific trade, Time Warner Inc debt was quoted one to two basis points tighter following the release of strong fourth-quarter earnings, traders said. The company also projected a record setting performance for itself in 1997.

Still, activity all around was suppressed by the $39.75 billion in U.S. government supply to hit the market between Tuesday and Thursday. Government bonds ended little changed on the day as players digested $17.75 billion three-year notes auctioned on Tuesday afternoon.
Demand at the first auction was termed by several traders as "fairly good."
Light new issuance included $100 million senior notes from St. Paul Bancorp, priced as 7-1/8s to yield 7.21 percent or 93 basis points over Treasuries via lead manager Keefe, Bruyette & Woods Inc.
A few bid lists circulated the Street loaded with shorter duration paper, said one trader at a big New York shop.
